items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.
items.title: PGAA: a claim-state compiler for perturbation-transcriptomic evidence

items.summary: This record contains the first Lean-verified certificate in the Quantum–Classical Shared-Time working formalization series. Q1 establishes a common real-time mathematical structure for quantum and classical evolution. The certificate places both systems on the same time domain, formally represents their evolving states and time derivatives, and proves that when quantum and classical states correspond through an observation map at every time, their accumulated change between two times also corresponds exactly. The formalization includes normalized quantum-state evolution, classical phase-state evolution, shared-time structure, derivative uniqueness, and an orientation-independent change result that works in either direction between two times. This first milestone is intentionally foundational. It establishes the formal structure needed for the later quantum-to-classical bridge without yet assuming the Schrödinger equation, Ehrenfest theorem, Newtonian dynamics, or the later Chronos connection. The next stage is to formalize quantum expectation values and their time evolution as the next step toward a machine-checked Ehrenfest bridge connecting accepted quantum mechanics with accepted classical physics. This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. The certificate package includes Lean source, reproducibility instructions, dependency and provenance documentation, build information, axiom audits, and checksums. The formal build passes without sorry, admit, or sorryAx placeholders.

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.

We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
items.title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.
items.title: PGAA: a claim-state compiler for perturbation-transcriptomic evidence

items.summary: This repository contains the curated 17-specimen compression summary, source-file checksum manifest, deterministic analysis code, machine-readable statistical outputs, sensitivity analyses, regenerated figures, data dictionary and provenance documentation supporting the manuscript “Failure-Sensitive Manufacturing Heterogeneity in Pultruded Unidirectional Carbon/Vinyl-Ester Composites: A Reproducible Open-Data Reanalysis”. The source experimental data are openly archived at Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18435237) and are not duplicated here. An optional downloader verifies all source files by MD5 before independent header re-extraction. The reanalysis compares three pultruded profiles from the same carbon-fiber/vinyl-ester base material and tests whether profile-level manufacturing heterogeneity is amplified in compression failure quantities relative to longitudinal stiffness.
items.title: Reproducibility Dataset and Code for Failure-Sensitive Manufacturing Heterogeneity in Pultruded Unidirectional Carbon/Vinyl-Ester Composites
